newsitem.title: UK: UK government EU policy will not change - Mawhinney.
newsitem.headline: UK government EU policy will not change - Mawhinney.

text.p: The government will not yield to pressure within the ruling Conservative Party to rule out British membership of a single European currency ahead of the election, party chairman Brian Mawhinney said on Tuesday.

"Government policy has been set out by the Cabinet, by the Prime Minister, by a number of us time and time again. It is not going to change," he told BBC television in an interview in Bournemouth where the party's annual conference starts today.
"It is not going to change because it is in the best national interest that we should make the decision on the single currency when all of the information is available."
Mawhinney said he believed the issue of Europe could be a plus for the Conservatives at the general election which must be held by next May.

"The election issue will be that the Labour Party and the Liberal Democrats are in favour of a federal Europe. This party is not in favour of a federal Europe, and on that we will be much closer to the views of the British people," he said.
Mawhinney also dismissed press reports speculating about the reasons behind the resignation of Conservative MP James Cran as an aide to Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Patrick Mayhew.
He said he had talked to Cran, who is abroad, on the telephone. "He wanted me to say on his behalf that he supports the government and there is no disagreement on policy," he said.
He said Cran had stepped down to give himself more time to familiarise himself with the new constituency he is to fight at the election.
